scenario: A cruise-industry report features only excursion operators that survive multiple seasons and maintain customer-satisfaction above 95%. Buyers use the featured average to estimate typical satisfaction across all operators.

data.description: Only surviving operators with satisfaction above 95% are featured. Satisfaction is Normal with sigma 3 percentage points.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean satisfaction mu across all operators and (b) the fraction of operators featured.
naive_answer: Typical satisfaction is about 96.3% because that is the report average.
naive_trap: Only unusually successful surviving operators are included.
reasoning_trace: Use the lower-truncated normal model with alpha around 1.5.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(95-mu)/3; return mu+3*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-96.32
mu=brentq(eq,0,94.99)
frac=norm.sf((95-mu)/3)
assert abs(mu-90.5)<0.3 and abs(frac-0.0668)<0.005
